messages:
oncall-bot: INCIDENT OPENED (sev-2) — autoscaling-paged-attn on gpu-cluster-prod started seeing progressive memory fragmentation, multiple containers restarting. Link: https://redwood.incidents/2312345678 :rotating_light:

raj: seeing repeated container restarts on gpu-7, OOMs with CUDA driver messages. Replica count dipped from 12 -> 6 in 7m. :eyes:

kate: metrics from dd: latency p95 + 1200ms for serving route /v1/generate, error rate 502 -> 4.6%. Affected customers: a few high-throughput PLG teams.

mike: past 2 hours we have a slow mem creep on the paged-attn allocator. GC/eviction not keeping up with new KV pages. Node-level dmesg shows oom_killer invoked. Snippet:

```
[ 1234.567890] Out of memory: Killed process 4321 (redwood-runtime) total-vm:3456784kB, anon-rss:2893120kB, file-rss:0kB
[ 1234.567896] CUDA: GPU 0: memory allocation failed: out of memory
```

raj: also seeing repeated cudaErrorLaunchFailure logs during attention paging ops. Suspect a race where fragment table grows and then allocation fails, leading to partial KV state causing crash loops.

sara: triage checklist updated in runbook: https://runbooks.internal/paged-attn-memcreep. Steps attempted so far: bumped eviction threshold, cordoned gpu-7, scaled down batch size for the staging config, restarted runtime on the node. Short-term effect: reduced crash frequency by ~30%.

eng-runtime: proposed hotfix PR 5123 to add aggressive page compaction + defensive allocation guard. Patch includes: reduce prefetch window, force compact on allocator every N allocations, and circuit-breaker for allocation failure to trigger immediate fallback to smaller KV layout.

kate: customers impacted: - org-alpha: 22% 500s on inference path - org-beta: elevated latency causing queuing timeouts. We should prepare a customer note. Support-ops, can you start triage on affected accounts and flag exec contacts?

support-ops: on it. Messaging draft: "We're investigating an infrastructure issue affecting model generation latency and errors for some customers. Root cause under investigation; will provide updates within 30 minutes."

raj: immediate mitigation idea: enable cross-node KV-sharing disabled (temp) and force per-request smaller sequence chunking to limit page growth. I can roll a runtime config change to the affected pool (canary) if we want to test. :+1:

mike: canary config and live patch plan: 1) apply runtime flag --kv-page-compact=1 --kv-prefetch=0.2 to canary subset (2 nodes) 2) watch OOM/restart rate for 10m 3) if stable, roll to the rest 4) if not, revert and drain nodes.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: canary/runtime-config-update to pool/gpu-prod-canary by raj at 2312345800. CI: green.

raj: rolling canary now. `kubectl set env deployment/redwood-runtime -n redwood-prod --env="KV_PAGE_COMPACT=1,KV_PREFETCH=0.2"`

(5m later)

raj: canary runtime restarted, initial logs show compaction cycles triggered. Crash loop count on canary nodes dropped from 4/min -> 0.6/min. :tada:

kate: telemetry shows p95 latency on canary improved by 350ms, error rate down to 1.2% for those nodes. Good sign.

mike: recommending progressive rollout. Add an additional tolerance check: if crash rate <1/min and error rate delta <1% then continue. Also need to temporarily disable attention-paged prefetching on the larger queues to avoid sudden load.

eng-runtime: noting the compaction is heavier CPU-wise; may increase CPU usage and slightly impact throughput. We'll keep an eye. Also instrumented a new metric: kvcache_fragment_ratio (available in dd).

sara: plan for next 60m: 1) progressive rollout to 50% of pool 2) prepared incident customer note 3) postmortem and RCA on allocation race 4) coordinate with infra for possible kernel upgrade if dmesg shows driver-level leak.

support-ops: customer note posted to status page and alerted top 5 affected customers. Slack DM to partner success sent.

(20m later)

kate: rollout at 50% completed. Some nodes showing higher CPU but still stable. Error rate for overall pool down to 1.7%. Preparing to continue to 100% in 15m if no regressions.

raj: live mitigation checklist executed: drained 2 worst nodes, cordoned, restarted runtime with compacting flag. Node rejoin looks healthy.

mike: follow-up actions assigned: - eng-runtime (mike) -> prioritize allocator refactor sprint (PR 5230) to avoid fragmentation growth - eng-sre (raj) -> add automated circuit-breaker that caps per-request KV growth - infra (kate) -> gather kernel/CUDA driver logs and check for memory leak patterns

eng-runtime: added temporary alert: kvcache_fragment_ratio > 0.65 for >10m -> page-eviction escalation.

sara: assigning postmortem owner: mike. Postmortem target publish ETA: 72h.

support-ops: status update posted: "Mitigation in progress; rolling fix applied to majority of nodes. Some customers may still see intermittent errors. Next update in 30m."

(incident updated -> monitoring continued)
